content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide and mycophenolate: Aluminum hydroxide can reduce the levels or effectiveness of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH, which affects absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To minimize this effect, separate the administration of these drugs by at least 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 2. Aluminum hydroxide and nadolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases nadolol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction is specific to oral forms. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 3. Aluminum hydroxide and nebivolol: Similar to nadolol, aluminum hydroxide reduces nebivolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies to oral forms. Separate doses by 2 hours and monitor closely. 4. Neomycin and magnesium hydroxide: Neomycin can decrease magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. This is considered a minor interaction with unknown clinical significance. Monitor closely if co-administered. 5. Aluminum hydroxide and neratinib: Aluminum hydroxide decreases neratinib levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing its absorption. This interaction applies to oral forms. Separate antacid and neratinib dosing by 3 hours, modify therapy as needed, and monitor closely. 6. Aluminum hydroxide and nilotinib: Aluminum hydroxide reduces nilotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. To avoid this interaction, administer antacids 2 hours before or after nilotinib. Monitor closely and consider modifying therapy. 7. Aluminum hydroxide and nimodipine: Aluminum hydroxide increases nimodipine levels by raising gastric pH, potentially leading to increased effects or toxicity. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Aluminum hydroxide and nisoldipine: Similar to nimodipine, aluminum hydroxide increases nisoldipine levels by altering gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Aluminum hydroxide and nitrenedipine: Aluminum hydroxide increases nitrenedipine levels by raising gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Aluminum hydroxide and nitrofurantoin: Aluminum hydroxide decreases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 11. Magnesium hydroxide and nitrofurantoin: Magnesium hydroxide also reduces nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Monitor closely. 12. Magnesium hydroxide and ofloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases ofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 13. Aluminum hydroxide and ofloxacin: Aluminum hydroxide reduces ofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, separate doses by 2 hours. 14. Aluminum hydroxide and omadacycline: Aluminum hydroxide decreases omadacycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair tetracycline absorption, reducing efficacy. 15. Magnesium hydroxide and omadacycline: Magnesium hydroxide also reduces omadacycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 16. Magnesium hydroxide and oxytetracycline: Magnesium hydroxide decreases oxytetracycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Aluminum hydroxide and oxytetracycline: Aluminum hydroxide reduces oxytetracycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Separate doses by 2 hours. 18. Aluminum hydroxide and pamidronate: Aluminum hydroxide decreases pamidronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 19. Magnesium hydroxide and pancrelipase: Magnesium hydroxide may reduce the effects of pancrelipase through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as antacids may negate the beneficial effects of enzymes. 20. Paromomycin and magnesium hydroxide: Paromomycin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. This is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Monitor closely. 21. Aluminum hydroxide and pazopanib: Aluminum hydroxide decreases pazopanib levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing its absorption. Avoid co-administration or use short-acting antacids instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists. Separate antacid and pazopanib dosing by several hours. 22. Magnesium hydroxide and pazopanib: Magnesium hydroxide also reduces pazopanib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Aluminum hydroxide and penbutolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases penbutolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 24. Magnesium hydroxide and penicillamine: Magnesium hydroxide reduces penicillamine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 25. Aluminum hydroxide and penicillamine: Aluminum hydroxide decreases penicillamine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 26. Aluminum hydroxide and perindopril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of perindopril through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Aluminum hydroxide and pexidartinib: Aluminum hydroxide decreases pexidartinib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 28. Magnesium hydroxide and pexidartinib: Magnesium hydroxide also reduces pexidartinib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 29. Simethicone and pexidartinib: Simethicone decreases pexidartinib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 30. Aluminum hydroxide and pindolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases pindolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 31. Aluminum hydroxide and polysaccharide iron: Aluminum hydroxide decreases polysaccharide iron levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Magnesium hydroxide and ponatinib: Magnesium hydroxide reduces ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Aluminum hydroxide and ponatinib: Aluminum hydroxide decreases ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Aluminum hydroxide and posaconazole: Aluminum hydroxide decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Magnesium hydroxide and potassium phosphates (IV): Magnesium hydroxide reduces the effects of potassium phosphates by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Aluminum hydroxide and propranolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases propranolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by 2 hours. 37. Use caution, especially with frequent or high-dose antacids. 38. Aluminum hydroxide and quinapril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of quinapril through an unspecified mechanism.
